input.question: How does the energy required to enrich fissile material compare to the energy released in reactors and bombs?
input.ground_truth: Enrichment activity is in weird units called "SWU" (separative work units). There's a bunch of useful info here: _URL_0_ The example at the end is especially helpful. It says that to enrich enough uranium to power eight 1300 MW power plants, you need an enrichment plant with a capacity of about 1 million SWU per year. Also from that article: > gas centrifuge plants require just 50 to 60 kW·h (180–220 MJ) of electricity per SWU. That adds up to 50-60 gigawatt-hours for the enrichment plant. The eight reactors would produce roughly 100,000 gigawatt-hours of electricity. So you end up with about 2,000 times as much energy out as you put in. A huge win. What about World War 2 fission bombs? Oak Ridge used a different enrichment technology, gaseous diffusion rather than centrifuges, which are at least 50 times less efficient. That, plus the extra work required to enrich uranium to bomb levels, might account for the huge use of electricity for the Manhattan project.
